# deed_relationship (Resource)

A relationship between two entities, **asserted through the provider's source** (`terraform` by default). Several sources can assert the same relationship (for example an importer and Terraform); this resource manages only the provider's assertion: it is treated as gone when that assertion is missing or no longer live, and destroying the resource retracts only that assertion — the relationship stays while other sources still assert it.

Cross-project relationships need a bridge between the projects (or a `bridge` entity endpoint).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Endpoints by entity ID …
resource "deed_relationship" "jellyfin_runs_on_pve" {
  type = "runs_on"
  from = { id = deed_entity.jellyfin.id }
  to   = { id = deed_entity.pve.id }
}

# … or by kind and name (the declaring project is then required).
resource "deed_relationship" "ups_powers_nas" {
  project    = deed_project.homelab.name
  type       = deed_relationship_type.powers.name
  from       = { kind = "example.com/ups", name = "ups-01" }
  to         = { kind = "server", name = "nas-01" }
  attributes = jsonencode({ outlet = 3 })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `from` (Attributes) Source endpoint. Set `id`, or `kind` and `name` (plus `project` for an entity in another project). Changing it forces a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--from))
- `to` (Attributes) Target endpoint. Set `id`, or `kind` and `name` (plus `project` for an entity in another project). Changing it forces a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--to))
- `type` (String) Relationship type, built-in (`runs_on`, `hosted_on`, `depends_on`, `owned_by`, …) or custom (`deed_relationship_type`). Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `attributes` (String) Relationship attributes as a JSON object string (use `jsonencode`), validated against the type's attributes schema. Compared semantically.
- `project` (String) Project (name or ID) of the declaring source. Defaults to the project of the `from` entity; required when `from` is addressed by kind and name. Changing it forces a new resource (the same project by name or ID does not). Import records the project ID.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Relationship ID (`rel_…`).
- `project_id` (String) ID (`prj_…`) of the relationship's project (the `from` entity's project).

<a id="nestedatt--from"></a>
### Nested Schema for `from`

Optional:

- `id` (String) Entity ID (`ent_…`), e.g. `deed_entity.x.id`.
- `kind` (String) Entity kind.
- `name` (String) Entity name.
- `project` (String) Project name or ID of the entity when it is addressed by kind and name in another project.


<a id="nestedatt--to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `to`

Optional:

- `id` (String) Entity ID (`ent_…`), e.g. `deed_entity.x.id`.
- `kind` (String) Entity kind.
- `name` (String) Entity name.
- `project` (String) Project name or ID of the entity when it is addressed by kind and name in another project.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import deed_relationship.jellyfin_runs_on_pve rel_01m5qxaz4gert82x56sfvwszmw # relationship ID
```
